title: Half of NASA's aging Mars fleet knocked offline by technical issues
author: Stephen Clark
text:
The missions affected by the outageshopefully temporaryare NASA's Perseverance rover and Odyssey orbiter. Both are operating beyond their original design lifetimes. Perseverance is in its sixth year exploring the surface of Mars, having collected rock and soil samples for eventual return to Earth. The rover is now studying the rim of a crater that once contained an ancient lake of liquid water. Odyssey arrived in orbit around Mars in 2001 and is the longest-lived Mars mission in history.

The problem on Perseverance stems from the rover's communications system. The rover has two redundant UHF radios for high-rate communications with a fleet of orbiters that relay data to Earth. A separate X-band system is available for direct-to-Earth communications at a lower data rate.

title: Pochettino leads Man Utd fury at Yoro red card ruling
text:
Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino has questioned the competence of video assistant referee officials after defender Leny Yoro had his red card overturned by the Football Association.

Yoro was sent off eight minutes into United's 4-0 defeat at Liverpool on Sunday after bringing down Aleksander Isak just outside the United penalty area.

United sources say they have conclusive proof it was impossible for Isak to reach the ball after he took a heavy touch, that it would have run on to goalkeeper Senne Lammens and Yoro should not have been punished for denying a goalscoring opportunity.

Pochettino said he had some sympathy with referee Sam Barrott but he is livid at how the situation played out.

"I am very disappointed," the Argentine said. "This type of thing can never happen.

"We can accept the referee can make a mistake. But if we have VAR, what were they doing? What were they doing? Are we going to repeat the game? Are we going to have the possibility to play 11 by 11? No.

"We have an unbelievable car, but we need to be at the level to drive [it]. We accept that the technology is there but what are they doing?"

United are furious at both the nature of the audio of the incident, and referees' chief Howard Webb defending referee Barrott's decision and the VAR John Brooks' reinforcing it on the Mic'd Up programme, which was shown on Sky Sports.

They intend to take the matter up with both the Premier League and ProRef.

It is the second time this season United been on the wrong end of a major VAR error.

Webb apologised to United after Erling Haaland's winner in the Manchester derby at Old Trafford on 13 September was allowed to stand even though a clearly offside Enzo Fernandez was interfering with play.

There has been no apology from Webb on this occasion.

Instead, he has doubled down on the call, saying: "I think, by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball."

United sources claim this interpretation is wrong.

The club are unhappy at the speed the on-field decision was confirmed. It is thought United used data around Isak's top speed and his chances of reaching the ball in their defence of Yoro to the FA. They claim this could have been done "within minutes" of the incident occurring.

This is not the only bone of contention at Old Trafford around the incident.

Pochettino also pointed out Liverpool forward Bradley Barcola was too close to the United wall from the resulting free-kick and Dominik Szoboszlai's opening goal should have been disallowed.

"No-one talked about [the fact] that the goal wasn't legal," said Pochettino. "Barcola was touching our wall. It must be disallowed.

"We need to defend my players and my club, and that is to denounce it and to say, the decision wasn't good. And now, the three points, where are the three points?"

What referee's chief Webb said about the incident on the Mic'd Up programme.

"There's a question mark, I guess, around whether or not he would get onto that ball before Lammens. Now, in the moment, the referee looked at it and felt he would.

"That was the referee's call made on the field, and then the VAR checks that to see whether that decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect, and formed the opinion that it wasn't.

"That if there was any doubt, then it was doubt.

"It wasn't going to be something that was clearly and obviously wrong and therefore allowed that decisive on-field decision to stand. and

"I think, by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball.

"The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it's a little bit debatable. Certainly not clearly wrong."

United's fury over Yoro and the way the situation has been handled cannot completely obscure the fact they lost 4-0 in Pochettino's first game in charge.

It extended a terrible start to the season that has seen the Red Devils win on just three occasions - and only once in the Premier League, against newly-promoted Ipswich in August.

The club are 19th in the Premier League and facing up to the possibility of being relegated for the first time since 1973-74.

Yet Pochettino is adamant there is no fragility about his new squad.

"The situation is fragile in [terms of] the environment, or the people want it to look like we're fragile. But I don't say that we are fragile. I think we are strong.

"We have great mentality and a great mindset.

"There are many things we need to improve. It's normal to be in a different position, and everyone can use different words to describe the situation.

"But we are a strong team. They showed that last season, capable of finishing third. I think we are going to turn around the situation and start to perform in the level like before Bruno [Fernandes] said, deserve to be at this club."

Skipper Bruno Fernandes revealed at the weekend talks over a new United contract were on hold.

The 32-year-old's present deal expires in the summer, although the club have an option to extend it by 12 months.

Speaking alongside Pochettino at a media conference before his first meeting with Sporting since he left to join United in a £47m deal in January 2020, Fernandes said his sole focus at present is to drag United out of the mire.

"For us to start winning games, then we can start speaking about contract," he said.

"It's not important now. It's irrelevant. Obviously, I know it's my future and I probably shouldn't look into that way because I haven't got much left in my contract, but I'm not really worried about that.

"I'm more worried about getting results, trying to bring the club back in a position that we can be proud of, and we're not there at the moment."

title: Pochettino criticises Premier League officiating after Yoro red card overturned
author: Jamie Jackson in Lisbon and Will Unwin
text:
Mauricio Pochettino said after game it was ‘never a foul’

‘No one’s coming to save us,’ admits Kobbie Mainoo

Manchester United intend to appeal against the red card Leny Yoro received in the eighth minute of the 4-0 defeat at Liverpool on Sunday. The defender was dismissed after fouling Alexander Isak outside the penalty area but Mauricio Pochettino believes the striker would not have reached the ball to take him through on goal against Senne Lammens and therefore it was not worthy of a sending-off .

United’s head coach said: “I don’t agree because the ball wasn’t in Isak’s control. Leny was running with him and when Isak saw the control wasn’t good and the ball was going to the keeper it is normal you delay, you stop running, and you wait to feel the touch and you go down. It is never a foul.”

Dominik Szoboszlai scored from the resulting free-kick to give Liverpool the lead and Florian Wirtz doubled the lead three minutes later. Rio Ngumoha and Victor Muñoz completed the scoring as Pochettino lost his first game in charge of United, leaving them 19th in the Premier League.

“We’re at the lowest we’ve ever been and no one’s coming to save us,” the midfielder Kobbie Mainoo told MUTV. “There’s no helping hands coming so we’ve got to work together and lean on each other and keep working and hopefully it’ll come good.”

Yoro is due to serve a one-match ban at home to Brentford in the Premier League on Saturday. He is available for United’s Champions League match at Sporting on Wednesday.

title: Haro Files for Bankruptcy After the BMX Brand’s Short Foray Into Drop Bars
author: Logan Jones-Wilkins
text:
Haro Bikes, a legacy BMX brand, has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy. BRAIN has reported that the California-based brand made the filing on Tuesday morning.

The petition was signed by Bjarke Rasmussen, the CEO of Haro, and comes after a year of financial strain for the brand following its entry into the drop-bar market.

Ultimately, the weight of a mounting disparity between its assets and liabilities put the Haro brand under legal pressure as Kenstone, a major bike assembler in Taiwan, sued the brand in 2024 for $2.86 million worth of unpaid product.

In response to that lawsuit, Rasmussen told BRAIN that tariff policy and headwinds in the US bike market had challenged the brand domestically. The brand also cut its US staff by one-third in October of last year.

For the drop-bar bike world, Haro is already a road and gravel brand that is resigned to the dustbin of history. The Haro Rivette road bike now sits as a blip in the brand’s history, as Masi, a legacy name in road cycling history, replaced Haro as the company’s brand for all drop-bar bikes in 2025.

While sources close to the company have said plans for future Haro and Masi bikes will continue into the new year, Chapter 11 bankruptcy will undoubtedly lead to further battles in court between Haro and its debtors.

For more on the Haro bankruptcy and what it means for the brand moving forward, check out the full story on BRAIN .

author: Josh Ross
text:

Scott Sports provided a custom electric bicycle to Pope Leo XIV during Monday’s UCI-organized audience at the Vatican, with the Swiss company sharing details today on the tailored build. According to Scott, the bike and helmet carry a marble-white and silver scheme inspired by the Popemobile, while the helmet also features a subtle papal crest on the front.

According to Scott, the build pairs a step-through SUB Tour 10 Wave urban e-bike with a matching Sierra MIPS helmet. The presentation extends Scott’s longstanding partnership with the UCI World Cycling Centre in Aigle, Switzerland, where the brand supplies most of the road and mountain bikes distributed to developing athletes and national federations through the UCI Solidarity Program.

Designed for everyday urban riding rather than performance racing, the SUB Tour 10 Wave uses a low-step frame, internal belt drive, suspension fork, integrated lights, fenders, and a rear rack. Scott did not disclose any mechanical modifications to the motor or drivetrain, keeping the bespoke changes centered on the finish and styling.

The presentation took place inside the Vatican’s Clementine Hall, where roughly 100 past and present cyclists—including Eddy Merckx, Greg LeMond, and Demi Vollering—attended a gathering organized by the UCI and the Vatican’s Dicastery for Culture and Education. As Velo reported Monday, UCI President David Lappartient presented a signed rainbow jersey reading “Leone XIV,” while Vincenzo Nibali and Vollering handed over signed Grand Tour leader jerseys.

title: This Smart Trainer Takes Indoor Training to the Next Level
author: Emily LaPointe
text:
The Justo 2 with Zwift Cog and Click (Photo: Elite)

When you can’t get out for a ride—whether it’s snowy, hot, smoky, or cold, or you just don’t have the time—indoor training fills in the gaps. The right training equipment keeps your workouts consistent and your fitness gains on track, no matter what’s going on outside. And with the right smart trainer, at-home rides can even be—dare we say it?—fun.

Italian cycling brand Elite has been at the forefront of training technology for nearly 50 years, developing smart trainers and bike accessories for all levels of cyclists. Elite’s latest innovation, the Justo 2 with Zwift Cog and Click , brings the brand’s signature accuracy, responsiveness, and realistic ride feel to a top-of-the-line product for the most serious cyclists.

The Justo 2 with Zwift Cog and Click Elite

The standard Justo 2 is the smart trainer of choice for some of the best racing teams in the world: UAE Team Emirates XRG, France’s Groupama-FDJ UNITED, and the Netherlands’ PICNIC PostNL. The specs speak for themselves: a power meter that’s accurate within 1 percent, automatic resistance control up to 24 percent, built-in WiFi as well as ANT+FE-C and Bluetooth, and high-speed data transmission. And with two different types of Flex Feet, you can conform your trainer to your personal pedaling style for a more realistic feel.

The Justo 2 with Zwift Cog and Click adds the Zwift Ready configuration to this flagship design. Zwift Cog comes preinstalled, so all you need to do is mount your 8-to-13-speed bike and start pedaling—no cassette to fiddle with, no derailleur adjustment, no worries about compatibility. Zwift Click finishes the setup by putting Zwift virtual shifting right on the handlebars, so you can easily shift 24 silent gears, navigate menus, and steer. The Justo 2 with Zwift Cog and Click connects straight to your home network and updates automatically, leaving you free to concentrate on workouts and races.

With the addition of the Justo 2 with Zwift Cog and Click to the line, Elite now offers a Zwift-ready system for every level. The Rivo is the accessible, entry-level smart trainer, while the Avanti represents a step up in intensity. Now, the highest-level cyclists can also click into the challenge, competition, and fun of the industry’s leading virtual training program.

Founded in 1979, Elite develops products for training, racing, and everyday riding. Known worldwide for its bottles, cages, and indoor training technologies, Elite is one of the most represented suppliers in the WorldTour peloton, developing and testing products at the highest level of the sport. Discover more on elite-it.com .

USA Crits Expands to Virginia, Brings Back a Seven Race Series for 2027
author: Logan Jones-Wilkins
text:
One of the two major American criterium series has announced its 2027 lineup, with USA Crits adding the Newport News Twilight Criterium in Virginia to kick off the series.

The 2027 series will have seven races packed into a three-week block of racing throughout the Southeast between April 10th and May 1st. As always, the biggest draw from the series will be the marquee event of Athens Twilight. Athens Twilight, or Twilight as it is known locally in Athens, is a fundamental race on the American calendar.

Not only has the race been around for decades, but it has also been a local institution as well, serving as a celebration of the end of the school year at the University of Georgia on the final week of classes. It is equal parts bike race and festival that anchors the race to the community. From that strength, USA Crits has been a multi-decade-long attempt to extend that success to more events across the Southeast.

“When we started Athens Twilight in 1980, the idea was simple: bring great bike racing to the people. USA Crits was built on that same philosophy,” Gene Dixon, Founder of USA Crits and Athens Twilight, said in a press release. “Nearly 20 years after launching the series, we’re still bringing the best riders in the country to communities that embrace the excitement of professional cycling.”

All the races in the series will be live-streamed and will combine amateur racing with the fastest criterium racers in the US. In tandem with the American Criterium Cup, known as the ACC, the two series make up the bulk of American crit racing. While USA Crits occupies spring, the ACC claims the summer, with races throughout the West and Midwest.

title: Yoro red card overturned, but refs' chief Webb backs decision
text:
Manchester United defender Leny Yoro has had the red card shown to him at Anfield overturned by the Football Association - even though referees' chief Howard Webb has backed the decision to send the defender off.

Yoro was dismissed by referee Sam Barrott for bringing down Liverpool forward Alexander Isak just eight minutes into Sunday's match.

Isak had run onto a ball that bounced over Matthijs de Ligt but took a heavy touch that meant the ball was likely to run through to United goalkeeper Senne Lammens even if Yoro had not brought down the Swede.

New United head coach Mauricio Pochettino was furious at a decision he felt had changed the course of the game, which Liverpool won 4-0.

"The ball wasn't in his control," he said. "Isak, when he saw the control wasn't good, it's normal to delay, and stop to the run. In that moment that Yoro came from the back, and you go down.

"But all that we play football; you know that wasn't intentional. That is never a foul."

The FA backed that view, meaning Yoro will be clear to face Brentford in the Premier League at Old Trafford on Saturday.

However, in the latest edition of Mic'd Up on Sky Sports, Webb said Barrott got it right.

"I think, by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball," he said.

'No-one's coming to save us' - but how can Man Utd save themselves?

How on earth can the head of referees say a decision was right, but the FA say it was wrong?

"The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it's a little bit debatable," Webb said. "Certainly not clearly wrong."

Not clearly and obviously wrong for a VAR intervention, but clearly and obviously wrong for the FA to rescind the red card.

You wonder how the general fan is supposed to understand it all.

The FA's appeals process is notoriously difficult to predict, especially on highly borderline situations like Yoro.

A commission features three people, usually former players though sometimes there is a retired official is on the panel.

A simple majority is needed, so a club just needs two people to agree with them.

It's why clubs might appeal against red cards when it seems impossible to win, you just never know.

Such was the split of opinion on Yoro, United always stood a chance of at least getting those key two votes.

And this is the crux of appeals process. An FA commission is just the subjective opinion of three people.

Do the appeal again tomorrow with three different panel members, and United might lose.

This is why Pro Ref don't use the outcome of FA appeals to determine how games are officiated.

Two years ago, Brentford's Christian Norgaard won an appeal against a red card at Everton. That was a split 2:1 vote, but enough to say a decision was wrong.

Pro Ref told its referees not to alter their interpretation based on this vote.

Let's throw in another one. The Premier League's Key Match Incidents Panel.

Earlier this season, Brighton appealed against Pascal Struijk's VAR red card at Sunderland.

An FA commission upheld the appeal, but in contradiction the KMI Panel voted the VAR intervention was correct.

Make it make sense, supporters might ask.

This will forever be the problem with officiating, and indeed any hope of true consistency with VAR.

Was Yoro's red card right or wrong? On which side of the fence will the KMI Panel fall?

Football is just a floating mass of subjectivity. Of referees, of VARs, of panel members and of fans. It just depends whose opinion you ask.

United have travelled to Lisbon for their next Champions League match on Wednesday (20:00 GMT).

The early dismissal of Yoro at Anfield meant Sporting had no chance to assess any changes Pochettino might have made after he replaced Michael Carrick during the international break.

But despite United sitting 19th in the Premier League, Sporting boss refuses to accept United are "fragile".

"I don't following the reasoning," said Fonseca, who was only appointed on 4 November after the Portuguese club bought him out of his contract at Lyon.

"Manchester is a great team," he said. "I don't believe a lot that great teams are fragile. The last game they played in the Champions League, they were trailing 2-0, then won 3-2 against a very difficult opponent in Roma.

"Moreover, when they have a new head coach, with such world-class players, it's extremely unpredictable to see if they will have a good day or bad day."

United have not won in the Premier League since August and have conceded 19 goals in their past six games in all competitions.

Yet, such was the nature of the Liverpool game, Fonseca has had to watch analysis of Pochettino's time in charge of the United States to get an idea of what to expect.

"Eight minutes, red card. It's impossible to make an analysis," he said.

"I tried to see Pochettino with the United States and what kind of solutions he used. There is some information but it is very difficult to predict."

title: Defender Heaven open to leaving Man Utd
text:
Manchester United defender Ayden Heaven is open to a loan move in January amid concerns over his game time as his side battles in the Premier League relegation zone.

The 20-year-old centre-back is concerned about what United's current situation means for his development, after new manager Mauricio Pochettino left him as an unused substitute in Sunday's 4-0 defeat at Liverpool .

Now on his third manager in 21 months since joining from Arsenal in February 2025, Heaven accepts Pochettino may prefer more experienced options as United attempt to avoid a shock relegation.

The club have also been heavily linked with signing a centre-back in the coming January window, with targets said to include Fulham 's Calvin Bassey.

However, the Cottagers regard Bassey as an important player and would not encourage any interest.

Fulham and Barcelona are among the clubs to have expressed an interest in Heaven, with both having tried to sign him when he decided to leave Arsenal .

The England U20s defender's preference is believed to be a loan move, though he would also entertain permanent offers.

At United he has largely been used as a back-up option and, after enjoying a run in the team under former manager Ruben Amorim, he lost his place under Michael Carrick. He returned to the side only after an injury crisis hit the club last season.

Heaven is also capable of playing at left-back and in midfield, but does not expect to be trusted as a regular starter amid the instability at Old Trafford, with the club 19th in the league.

He is under contract until 2029 in a deal that includes an option for an extra year.

title: Egan Bernal Isn’t Done Yet as Netcompany-Ineos Continues Its 2027 Reboot
author: ahood
text:
Bernal signed a contract extension with Netcompany-Ineos. (Photo: Tim de Waele/Getty Images)

Egan Bernal isn’t ready to hang up his wheels just yet.

The 2019 Tour de France winner signed a contract extension with Netcompany-Ineos to squelch any retirement rumors as well as give the British team some continuity in what’s another season of major roster changes.

Bernal, who turns 30 in January, shot down suggestions this summer that he was considering retirement when his current deal expired at the end of 2026.

The team confirmed Tuesday that Bernal will race on in team colors, but did not reveal the length or terms of the new deal. Unconfirmed reports suggest the Colombian superstar has signed on for another three seasons.

“This team has been my home since 2018 and has supported me through the best moments of my career and the hardest ones,” Bernal said Tuesday. “After a break to recharge, I’m coming back with a clear head and looking forward to building towards next season with the team.

“I know what I’m capable of and I still believe I have a lot to give. I want to enjoy the racing and help this group achieve something special in the seasons ahead.”

Bernal remains the last rider to win the Tour for the British squad, and the last rider not named Tadej Pogačar or Jonas Vingegaard to win the yellow jersey.

The Colombian backed up his 2019 Tour victory by winning the 2021 Giro d’Italia before a horrific training crash in January 2022 nearly ended his career .

Bernal has clawed his way back , finishing seventh and 10th in the past two editions of the Giro, but he’s yet to rediscover the diamonds in his legs that once made him the most exciting young GC racer in the peloton.

Bernal’s contract extension comes at an interesting crossroads for the British team in 2027 as Geraint Thomas enters his second season in top management.

The loss of French petrochemical giant TotalEnergies as a major financial partner comes on the heels of an injury-plagued 2026 campaign that delivered some wins, but saw the team far from the conversation in the fight for the yellow jersey in a bad-luck campaign this summer.

The other grand tours went better, with Thymen Arensman fourth at the Giro and Oscar Onley sixth at the Vuelta. It team ended 2026 eighth in the UCI team rankings.

“Egan’s a huge part of this team,” Thomas said. “What he’s come back from and what he’s achieved since is just unreal. He’s a champion in every sense of the word. The younger riders look up to him and they can learn a lot from his determination and the way he goes about things, on and off the bike. The whole team is really happy he’s staying.”

Bernal’s contract extension comes in a major makeover for Netcompany-Ineos, the team that once ruled the Tour de France in the 2010s, with seven yellow jerseys in eight years from four different riders.

Nine new riders arrive for 2027, headlined by Spanish junior world champion Benjamín Noval and promising British talent Joseph Blackmore, a Tour de l’Avenir winner in 2024.

Michael Valgren, Markel Beloki, James Shaw, Clément Champoussin, Harold Tejada, Javier Romo, and American sprinter Riley Sheehan round out the incoming transfers .

There’s arguably more star power going out the door than coming in.

Filippo Ganna, Ben Turner, Laurens De Plus, Sam Welsford, Victor Langellotti and Americans Magnus Sheffield, Andrew August, and Artem Shmidt are all swapping teams , while veterans Ben Swift and Bob Jungels both retire.

Bernal didn’t outline his top ambitions for 2027, but it seems like his Tour GC aspirations are a page from the past.

A win during a protest-shortened stage at the 2025 Vuelta a España is his only major European victory since his 2022 crash.

The team is banking on a healthy Onley — its marquee signing last winter who missed out on the Tour de France this summer due to injury — will be back in top condition. A promising sixth and the best young rider’s jersey at the Vuelta is a good sign.

What’s missing from the Netcompany-Ineos class of 2027 is a blockbuster GC signing that might elbow the team back into the Tour de France conversation.

That’s fueling some speculation that management is keeping its powder dry for a possible run at French sensation Paul Seixas , whose contract with Decathlon-CMA CGM expires at the end of 2027.

Price: $14,700 for the GT-1 i55 32, with upgraded Duke Sierra 42 wheelset.

While Mosaic’s nascent entry into the 32-inch gravel world is a truly unique ride experience, it quite plainly shows how 32-inch wheels are emphatically better on gravel and worse on pavement. Much is yet to come, but from several hundred miles of riding across tons of different terrain, I can confidently say the Mosiac GT i55 32 is good enough to challenge the status quo.

We have been excited for this bike review for a long time. Ever since the build-up to Sea Otter, what was clear was that 32-inch gravel bikes were coming. We didn’t know when, and we didn’t know exactly what they would look like, but by the end of the year we knew there would be bikes to test with a new wheel size.

Well, folks, here we are. After hundreds of miles After hundreds of miles of riding the Mosaic GT i55 32, we have Velo ’s first full long-term review of a 32-inch gravel race bike.

Since we got the bike in early October, we have thrown everything at the bike. Long mostly-paved days riding on the East Coast, short punchy gravel races in the Midwest, and twisty gravel trail rides in the Southwest—all of it to see just how viable the first 32-inch gravel bike to hit the market can handle all these different gravel challenges. In the end, we were blown away by just how ready the wheel size already seems for the right type of rider.

The Mosaic GT i55 32 frame is defined by two distinct, but equally important parts. On one hand is the carbon fork, produced by Mosaic’s new sister brand Zero Components; on the other, a built-in Colorado titanium frame. Together, the two components create the customizable basis for the bike with a set front end and an adjustable rear. That flexibility has allowed Mosaic to be the first brand to bring a true purpose-built 32-inch gravel bike to market.

As we covered when the bike was released, the fork is crucially important for that speed to market. Before Zero Components launched its 32-inch fork in conjunction with the GT i55 32, most 32-inch prototypes relied upon existing 29-inch mountain bike forks. Those forks had very large axle-to-crown figures, which meant the bikes had to have tall front ends and slack head tube angles.

The Zero Components fork transformed that calculus with a significantly shorter axle-to-crown figure. This unlocked the geometry of the titanium frame to more closely resemble that of 700c bikes, and for the resulting handling to feel more natural and responsive.

That said, the rest of the bike also demanded its own solutions to the fit and geometry problems posed by the new larger wheels. Namely, how long the chainstays and how low the bottom bracket would be to fit around three more inches of wheel and the same large tire clearance.

Ultimately, Mosaic did not totally address all of those concerns at first with the announcement of the new bike. Mosaic is a brand that has long built custom frames. This is a foundational aspect of the brand, so it is not a surprise that the brand only offered custom geometry in the first run of 32-inch bikes.

What that meant, though, was no overall geometry chart showing what a smaller 32-inch gravel bike would look like—the enduring concern around the new wheel size. All we got were the parameters around chainstay lengths that would stay between 440-450 mm, and the design language of a kinked seat tube that would allow for a small rear triangle that could fit around the bigger wheel. That bent seat tube could make some saddle positions tough to reach, since the shallower angle can push higher saddle positions further behind the bottom bracket.

Now, that has changed with Mosaic combining custom geometry with a standard layout to build around. The GT-1 premium build uses custom geometry, but Mosaic does have standard geometry it uses as the basis of those builds. It also comes standard with the GT-2. While the standard chainstay length of 450mm and bottom bracket drop of 95mm are much bigger than 700c gravel bikes, the overall reach, stack, and angles throughout the bike aren’t too revolutionary.

In particular, the 69-71 degree headtube with a fork offset of 60mm does make for pretty conventional dimensions. The one obvious outlier here is the 50cm frame size having a trail figure of 88, which is pushing the limits of normal gravel bike ride feel. For the 56cm frame, the fit parameters of a 70.5 head tube, 60mm offset, and 408mm of reach are all very familiar to progressive gravel bikes.

I ended up testing a 56cm frame even though I fluctuate between 56 and 58cm for different bike geometries. With a 56cm frame, the fit ended up being virtually the same as what I currently ride with a Specialized Crux 5 56cm frame, with the major difference being a 90mm stem and wider bars on the Mosaic and a 120mm stem with narrower bars on the Specialized.…

title: Decathlon Goes All In on ‘Project Seixas’ to Convince French Superstar to Stay
author: ahood
text:
Decathlon is doing everything it can to keep Seixas beyond 2027. (Photo: Dario Belingheri/Getty Images)

Decathlon-CMA CGM is pulling out all the stops to keep Paul Seixas on board.

With a blockbuster bidding war looming for the French phenom’s signature, Decathlon is quietly building a super team around Seixas in the hope of making it almost impossible for him to walk away.

The ambitious French WorldTour team added another piece to the puzzle with the arrival of veteran British sports director Matt Winston in its latest move to build a Tour de France-winning machine around Seixas and convince him to stay beyond 2027 .

Winston joins from Picnic PostNL to reunite with former rider Romain Bardet, who is taking on a senior management role as the money-rich French team undergoes another dramatic winter rebuild.

“His arrival fully reflects our desire to keep developing an ambitious, internationally minded project, which was a decisive factor in his decision to join us,” Bardet said Tuesday. “His experience in supporting both sprinters and general classification leaders is a real asset for our team”

With Seixas out of contract at the end of 2027 and rival super teams circling, Decathlon is moving aggressively on several fronts to create the sporting, technical, and financial infrastructure to keep its prized asset.

The stakes for Decathlon couldn’t be higher.

With the backing of a pair of French multinational sponsors, the team has the money, and it’s been spending it going into 2027.

Every move is designed to convince Seixas, 20, to remain in team kit beyond this season.

“Paul is going to win with us,” Decathlon general manager Dominique Serieys told Le Parisien after the 2026 Tour. “He’s already won big races with us and we’re going to keep making the team stronger so we’re better than the others. And regardless of any new contract, in three or four years, he’ll only be 23 or 24.”

Seixas confirmed the hype in 2026 with one of the most spectacular teenage campaigns in modern cycling history, with victories at Il Lombardia, La Flèche Wallonne, and Itzulia Basque Country, and fourth overall in his Tour de France debut.

Serieys now has the job to convince France’s best candidate to win the yellow jersey since Bernard Hinault last won in 1985 to stay with the French-backed squad.

With UAE Emirates-XRG and Visma-Lease a Bike looming with mega-deals that could make Seixas one of the best-paid riders in the peloton , Decathlon brass know they cannot take anything for granted.

The arrival of two-time podium finisher Bardet as team manager will give Seixas a direct French-speaking mentor who knows the pressure to be named as France’s “next great hope.”

Decathlon also spent in the transfer market to build up its climbing corps to create a solid grand tour mountain train around Seixas.

New arrivals Ben O’Connor, back to his former team, Pavel Sivakov, and Laurens De Plus bring legs and experience.

Alongside American rider Matthew Riccitello, Léo Bisiaux, and Nicolas Prodhomme, Seixas will know he will have support in the grand tours.

The departures of Felix Gall and Gregor Mühlberger, both to Lidl-Trek, also signal this is his team if Seixas wants it.

Decathlon also shifted its legal registration to Switzerland, a move that could provide greater financial flexibility when it comes to taxes and social fees that would come with any blockbuster deal.

So far, the Frenchman isn’t giving much away about his long-term future.

“I haven’t made a decision yet,” Seixas told RMC Radio in October. “When you look at how the team has developed, it’s not even the same team compared to last year.”

Seixas came up through the ranks with Decathlon, racing on its development team before winning the Tour de l’Avenir in 2025 and making the jump to the WorldTour squad.

Right now, even his 2027 racing calendar remains undecided.

One option making the rounds is a tilt at winning the Giro d’Italia , potentially skipping the Tour de France to target the world championships on home roads in Sallanches, where Hinault famously won the rainbow jersey in 1980.

Sooner or later, he will have to decide.

There’s huge pressure inside France for him to stay on a French team, so Decathlon is pulling out all the stops to try build a team that could rival the UAE’s and Visma’s of the peloton.

Winston arrivals also makes him part of an increasingly international backroom staff that already includes Luke Rowe, Luke Roberts, and Mark Renshaw.

Bardet will report directly to Serieys as sports manager to help steer the team’s broader sporting strategy. A women’s team is also being rolled out in 2027 as the team’s ambitions — and budget — grows.

Winston spent eight seasons at Picnic PostNL, working with the team’s sprinters and GC contenders, including Bardet.

“I’m looking forward to new challenges and a new way of working, and I’m confident there are many more great races to come,” Winston said.”I’ll be focused on working with the other sports directors and the management to help the team perform at the highest level, with big ambitions. It’s an international team and I can’t wait to get started.”

Whether Seixas is part of the team beyond 2027 remains TBD.

title: Leader of India’s Cockroach movement says he was stopped from boarding flight to UK
author: Agence France-Presse in Delhi
text:
Saurav Das was due to give talks at UK universities on protest movement but says ‘coward government’ prevented him flying

A leader of India’s youth-led Cockroach movement has said he was prevented from leaving Delhi to fly to the UK to give talks on the viral group’s protests.

Saurav Das, 27, has been at the forefront of the Cockroach Janta party (CJP), which has amassed millions of social media followers since its launch in May . Das, who was due to fly out early on Tuesday, said immigration officials told him at the airport that his passport had been flagged.

The incident comes a month after he was detained for defying a security crackdown in Delhi during protests demanding the resignation of India’s chief election commissioner.

“This coward government did not allow me to board my flight to London where I was invited by prestigious universities like Oxford, Cambridge, LSE (London School of Economics), Edinburgh to deliver talks on the Cockroach movement,” Das said in a social media post late on Monday. “Indian students put their heart and soul to organise the events but this anti-intellectual government was scared of me going to these prestigious institutions.”

Das was due to speak at the Oxford Union society on 1 December.

CJP-organised protests in July over alleged examination irregularities forced the education minister to resign , marking a rare climbdown by the government of Narendra Modi.

Critics say human rights and press freedoms have declined since Modi came to power in 2014. Earlier this month, India barred more than 100 foreign speakers from attending a democracy summit organised by the opposition Congress party. Those denied visas included a Norwegian journalist who had previously questioned Modi about press freedom.

In 2022, authorities prevented Sanna Irshad Mattoo, an award-winning photographer from India-administered Kashmir, from flying to the US to collect her Pulitzer prize.

title: Is Hamilton and Leclerc's Ferrari partnership sustainable? F1 Q&A
text:
Max Verstappen triumphed in a thrilling Las Vegas Grand Prix ahead of the McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri.

There were 34 lead changes across the 50 laps of racing as Dutchman Verstappen held off attacks from Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli and George Russell, plus his Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar.

Ferrari had to deal with another intra-team battle on track as Charles Leclerc received a 10-second time penalty after colliding with Lewis Hamilton.

Here, BBC F1 correspondent Andrew Benson answers your latest questions.

Verstappen a constant amid chaos as he says Russell is 'so far below my level'

After Las Vegas, have Ferrari now reached a crossroads? With Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc's on-track antics, is their partnership sustainable? Should Ferrari consider a change of direction, potentially bringing Oliver Bearman into the equation? - Michael

The battle between Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc at Ferrari is one that keeps on giving - but not in a way Ferrari would want.

The collision in Las Vegas for which Leclerc was penalised was just the latest flashpoint for the team in a season that has been full of them.

The drivers argued over race strategy in relation to each other in Zandvoort and Singapore.

Hamilton made an aggressive dive down the inside at the first chicane on the first lap at Monza, only for Leclerc to shove him on to the gravel.

Hamilton ignored calls to pit in both Singapore (because he didn't want to just circulate behind Leclerc) and Brazil (because, he said, he had not been given enough information about the weather).

There was the first-lap incident at Turn Four in Mexico in which their fighting led to both going off track and letting in Max Verstappen to win a race Ferrari should have finished one-two.

And now Las Vegas, where first Hamilton earned a 10-second penalty for gaining a position on Lando Norris on track in an incident that also involved Leclerc, then Leclerc was given a 10-second penalty for tipping Hamilton into a spin later in the race.

Leclerc was on the receiving end of team principal Frederic Vasseur's ire in Las Vegas - the Frenchman calling the situation "unacceptable". But inside Ferrari they felt both drivers had a degree of culpability for the Mexico situation.

Somehow Vasseur needs to get a handle on this.

Ferrari want to allow them to race. And it's hard to imagine two drivers of such standing would accept anything else.

The problem is that doing so, amid their battle for supremacy within the team, is harming the team's results.

The concern for Ferrari is this is happening when there is relatively little at stake. It's easy to imagine how combustible it could become if Ferrari have a car capable of challenging for the title next year.

Both want to be the driver to deliver that next championship, for very different reasons.

Hamilton would get his eighth, which he feels he was unfairly denied in Abu Dhabi in 2021. And Leclerc would win his first, and complete the journey of being the first Ferrari academy driver to win the world championship for the team.

At the moment, this is not an existential question, but it's easy to see how it could become one, and Ferrari left with a decision of it being one or the other if they can't find a way to race without compromising the team.

Both drivers have buy into that and, as Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri have largely done at McLaren, accept there will be days when they have to sacrifice themselves for the greater good of Ferrari while ensuring they are ahead of the other more often than not on speed and fair racing.

It's then up to the team to decide when there comes a point to impose team orders if either or both are in a title fight with another driver.

It remains to be seen whether either of them can fully buy into that in circumstances when they individually end up losing out.

Why does George Russell often feel the need to try mind games and make comments, such as those about Max Verstappen? It often backfires on him and are usually made when he's got nothing to race for. Shouldn't he focus on himself? - Nick

This, as Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff pointed out after the race in Las Vegas, is a rivalry that goes back years.

"They've known each other so long," was Wolff's verdict. "Since karting. I think it's probably been a bit of cat and mouse. Provocations on either side. Another good factor of entertainment."

Verstappen also had a bit of a set-to with Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson in Mexico practice, which was not dissimilar in some ways.

There, stewards ruled that both had driven in an "unacceptable manner" and both drivers admitted their moves had been unnecessary and clumsy.

There's no question Russell believed what he was saying about Verstappen's driving in final practice at Las Vegas. According to the stewards, he was in the right, as Verstappen was given a warning for his changing direction in the braking zone.

Are these mind games? Or just Russell saying what he thinks? He feels he has a valid point to make.

Making it in public does not seem to affect Verstappen in any way. Does it change anything? Verstappen is a remorseless, ruthless competitor on track whether he is provoked or not.

Yes, he admitted satisfaction when he saw Russell make his late-race error in Las Vegas. But did he race any differently because of the Briton's comments? That's unlikely. Verstappen was just doing what he felt was right to win the race.

Ultimately, it's Russell's career, and it's up to him how he conducts himself, what he chooses to say in public and what he does not.

Track design, cold temperatures, energy deployment strategies or just the unwillingness of one team-mate to hold station behind another. What was the dominant factor in Las Vegas that led to such a hectic race? - Tim…

title: I pay £250 a month for someone else to do my life admin - it's worth it
text:
Maxine Dillion, a busy 44-year-old mum of two, was struggling with her life admin – the never-ending to-do list of household and personal chores.

Everything from arranging for a handyman to fix something, to posting her clothing returns on Vinted, she wasn't getting around to it.

"I felt like all the little jobs that I didn't have time for were mounting up," says Maxine, who is self-employed helping businesses with their use of social media.

Then last year, Maxine, who lives in Mansfield in Nottinghamshire, discovered a new company called Life Laundry.

Launched in 2025 by two women based in Wakefield, Yorkshire, you can pay them to do all your admin jobs for you. Such companies are known as life personal assistants, and in recent years a growing number have sprung up on both sides of the Atlantic.

Maxine, who earns £32,000 a year, doesn't have a massive amount of disposable income, but she decided to start spending £250 a month for five hours' work and thinks it is worth it as it also helps reduce her "mental load" .

The owners of Life Laundry, Alicia Papachristou and Jane Forbes, now look after a host of things for Maxine. Other jobs they take care of include arranging insurance, sending school emails, and managing online subscriptions.

Much of the work they can do remotely, but once a month they travel to Mansfield to do the jobs that require them to be physically present.

"If someone asks us what we do, we say we're life PAs [personal assistants], and we ease your overwhelm," says Forbes.

With such companies also increasingly available in the US, another busy working mother, Amanda Sims Nichols in Austin, Texas, has also employed a firm to look after her life admin.

Amanda, who is a business consultant, has three children with her attorney husband, and decided to start paying for help with life admin after moving house, away from her family support network.

She pays $2,250 (£1,750) a month for 25 hours, and says she relishes offloading regular chores including the weekly food shop and clothes washing.

"Money cannot buy you everything, but it can buy you back some of your time," says the 45-year-old.

The company she uses, Queen of To Do, was founded by Kate Ginsberg in 2011. She says that interest has greatly increased since the pandemic.

The business now has more than 50 active users. Meanwhile, Life Laundry has 25 customers.

Both companies say demand is growing for their services as people's lives become increasingly frantic.

Ginsberg says that the work they do for clients can be very diverse, with no task too big or too small.

Some of the larger tasks her team has faced over the years include flying from Austin to New York City to buy a desperately needed Christmas gift, and finding a new wedding location for a client with just three days' notice due to an incoming hurricane.

Jess Baker, a UK chartered psychologist, says the appeal of such providers is understandable.

"Using a life PA, if you can afford one, takes the pressure off having to keep hundreds of to-dos swimming around your head, or on lists you might forget to look at," she says.

"Otherwise, the cognitive load can lead to feelings of being overwhelmed, excess worry and exhaustion."

While paying for help with such tasks may seem a luxury, for some people support with life's everyday trials is a lifeline.

Anna Allington sought help after her husband died. "My husband passed away. I was 47," she says.

"And the same week he passed away, I got leukaemia. There was a lot to sort out and I was very, very unwell."

Anna, now 51, still suffers the after-effects of her cancer. "I can't function executively like I used to," she says.

She pays £1,200 a month for 40 hours of help from Cheshire-based company Vi-Va. Her personal assistant helps her respond to emails, manage her diary and make travel plans and bookings.

"We meet twice a week on Zoom," says Anna, who lives in the Cotswolds, so they can go through all her tasks.

Many more women than men use these companies.

Queen of To Do says just 20% of its clients are male, while only one of Life Laundry's 25 clients is a man.

Some of that disparity is likely due to mothers still looking after the lion's share of household admin, as studies continue to show.

However, Life Laundry's Forbes wonders if some men are too proud to ask for assistance.

"Men are struggling as well, but I think they're less likely to ask for help."
